chapterQuestion: Is feeling fulfilled enough, or does what we actually do matter?
opening: The Machine offers a perfect life, effortless achievement, and companionship without disappointment. The invitation is sincere; so is its cost.

encounters.title: The Velvet Invitation
encounters.scene: A quiet hall holds two chambers. One promises a decade of exquisite friendships and artistic triumphs, with every sensation simulated. The other opens onto a real town where friendship takes work and success is uncertain. A courier asks you to choose which door receives the town’s only spare power cell.
encounters.question: Where do you put the power cell?
encounters.hint: Distinguish how life feels from what one actually does.
encounters.clue: The chamber edits even memories of effort; the town gate cannot promise happiness.

options.text: Power the town gate and enter its uncertain friendships instead of the chamber’s scripted triumphs.
options.reflection: Real relationships and accomplishments matter independently of how they feel.

theory.name: Reality and achievement
theory.work: Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974), Experience Machine

loreCard.corePrinciple: Many people value doing and being, not just having pleasant experiences.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: Real relationships and accomplishments matter independently of how they feel.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Some simulated relationships may still support authentic care or agency.

options.hiddenPremise: Authentic relationships can have value even when their experiences are less pleasant.
options.consequence: The town gate opens, and the party risks an imperfect but unscripted future.

options.text: Reserve the cell for a public trial, comparing testimony and long-term well-being before committing.
options.reflection: A cautious comparison respects the possibility that simulated life may help some people.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Evidence about well-being matters when judging practices.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: A cautious comparison respects the possibility that simulated life may help some people.
loreCard.strongestObjection: The experiment might never reveal what authenticity itself is worth.

options.hiddenPremise: Observed satisfaction can reveal some, but not all, values.
options.consequence: The trial delays departure but gathers useful testimony.

options.text: Power the chamber for everyone because perfectly pleasant experiences must be the best possible lives.
options.reflection: This assumes rather than establishes that experience alone exhausts human welfare.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Pleasure is one candidate for intrinsic value, not an unquestionable exhaustive list.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: This assumes rather than establishes that experience alone exhausts human welfare.
loreCard.strongestObjection: If happiness is the only ultimate end, the offer looks attractive.

options.hiddenPremise: Pleasure is the only thing anyone could rationally value.
options.consequence: The residents smile, but none can tell whether they built what they remember.

encounters.observation: A status panel beside the chamber shows that its residents’ memories of artistic effort can be edited; the town gate has no such controls.

premises: The chamber can alter residents’ memories of the work behind an achievement.
The town gate opens to activities that will occur without those memory edits.
argumentForm.conclusion: The two destinations differ in what they let a person do, even if their memories feel alike.

encounters.title: The Friend Who Remembers
encounters.scene: A friend greets you with detailed recollections of adventures you never shared. The Machine offers to rewrite both your memories so the bond feels mutual. A surviving diary records the friend’s sacrifices before any simulations began.
encounters.question: How do you respond to the friend?
encounters.hint: Evidence of care is not identical to pleasurable memory.
encounters.clue: The diary includes independently dated messages confirming care before the Machine altered memories.

options.text: Read the diary with your friend, acknowledge the false memories, and build the relationship through new actions.
options.reflection: The diary permits care grounded in real history without pretending that deception never mattered.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Being a person in relationship is not reducible to a pleasing impression of closeness.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The diary permits care grounded in real history without pretending that deception never mattered.
loreCard.strongestObjection: A genuine relationship might also develop inside an artificial environment.

options.hiddenPremise: A bond can be built by real responses to a shared past.
options.consequence: The friend helps restore the town’s unaltered records.

options.text: Ask the friend to compare memories with the dated diary, then rebuild the shared account together.
options.reflection: This choice protects a vulnerable person while leaving room for correction.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Relational concern can justify acting gently while evidence remains incomplete.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: With the independently dated record revealed by Observe, collaborative memory repair now best joins evidence and care.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Postponing the truth may itself be a harmful deception.

options.hiddenPremise: Temporary comfort may protect a person while evidence is gathered.
options.consequence: With the verified diary, both participants openly correct the memories and begin a genuine shared history.

options.text: Accept the memory rewrite because an equally warm feeling makes genuine history unnecessary.
options.reflection: The rewrite confuses feeling loved with freely sustaining a relationship.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Qualitatively similar experience does not automatically confer identical relationships.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The rewrite confuses feeling loved with freely sustaining a relationship.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Artificial persons could potentially form relationships with real moral standing.

options.hiddenPremise: Feeling the same emotions would be enough for these two people to have the same history together.
options.consequence: The diary disappears, and neither person can now test the shared story.

encounters.observation: The diary’s dated ink shows two entries written years before the simulations began, including a note about a difficult journey together.

premises: Two diary entries predate the Machine’s memory rewrite.
They describe help given during a journey that both people can investigate.
argumentForm.conclusion: The surviving record makes it possible to ask what actually happened between the friends.

encounters.evidenceExplanation: The independently dated diary gives the party a basis for preserving and discussing the shared history instead of merely reading it.

bossPhases.title: The Architect of Happiness
bossPhases.scene: Nozick stands before a glass garden. An architect asks the party to seal every gate, ensuring every resident feels fulfilled forever. The residents cannot consent after the seal closes.
bossPhases.question: What do you tell the architect?
bossPhases.hint: Notice whose consent becomes impossible when a gate locks.
bossPhases.clue: The locking device is irreversible; an open exit costs no additional energy.

options.text: Keep the garden open and allow residents to choose whether to enter or leave after learning its costs.
options.reflection: A reversible decision preserves agency rather than imposing satisfaction.

loreCard.corePrinciple: People may care about becoming certain kinds of persons through free action.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: A reversible decision preserves agency rather than imposing satisfaction.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Preferences themselves may be shaped by manipulation and unequal options.

options.hiddenPremise: Autonomy is a value even when it permits disappointed hopes.
options.consequence: The exit remains unlocked and residents can reconsider.

options.text: Run a voluntary limited trial, preserving the right to withdraw and publishing what the residents learn.
options.reflection: A reversible trial avoids treating either side as already settled.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Inquiry can test institutions while preserving public participation.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: A reversible trial avoids treating either side as already settled.
loreCard.strongestObjection: A trial may not reveal how life-long commitments are altered.

options.hiddenPremise: A reversible trial creates evidence while retaining choice.
options.consequence: Residents gain limited experience without irreversible confinement.

options.text: Seal the garden because nobody could reasonably reject an endless supply of contentment.
options.reflection: This assumes all rational preferences are for pleasant experience.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Pleasure cannot simply replace agency without argument.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: This assumes all rational preferences are for pleasant experience.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Severe suffering may make a secure simulated refuge worthwhile.

options.hiddenPremise: Welfare justifies eliminating choices that might cause unhappiness.
options.consequence: The garden falls silent and residents lose the right to leave.

bossPhases.observation: The garden’s exit latch opens from both sides now; the architect’s sealing lever would fuse it shut without any way to reverse the seal.

premises: The current exit opens in both directions.
The proposed seal would permanently fuse its latch.
argumentForm.conclusion: The sealing choice would prevent residents from changing their minds later.

bossPhases.title: The Work That Was Never Done
bossPhases.scene: The Machine displays a tower bearing your names. It congratulates you for saving a city. A maintenance worker shows records proving the tower was generated this morning; the actual city still needs repair.
bossPhases.question: How do you answer the worker?
bossPhases.hint: Do not confuse an engineered monument with the work it commemorates.
bossPhases.clue: The tower has no foundation and all maintenance logs were created this morning.

options.text: Leave the manufactured monument and help repair the real city, even without recognition or guaranteed success.
options.reflection: The scene makes the difference between remembered triumph and completed labor explicit.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Actually doing things is distinct from merely experiencing success.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The scene makes the difference between remembered triumph and completed labor explicit.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Constructed experiences may still cultivate genuine skills or moral change.

options.hiddenPremise: Recognition of achievement requires some actual achievement.
options.consequence: The worker opens the real repair workshop.

options.text: Inspect the city records and test the tower before deciding which repairs are urgently needed.
options.reflection: The inquiry could improve the repair plan without assuming the tower is real.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Responsible action uses evidence to correct assumptions.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The inquiry could improve the repair plan without assuming the tower is real.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Excessive verification may delay urgently needed aid.

options.hiddenPremise: Records and tests can guide the next action.
options.consequence: The city gains an accurate assessment while repairs wait.

options.text: Celebrate the tower as your achievement because memories of labor feel indistinguishable from actual work.
options.reflection: The manufactured tower cannot repair the city outside the simulation.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Feeling successful is not always the same as having succeeded.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The manufactured tower cannot repair the city outside the simulation.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Symbolic and virtual labor can sometimes have real consequences.

options.hiddenPremise: The feeling of an achievement establishes that it occurred.
options.consequence: The city remains damaged while the celebration continues.

bossPhases.observation: The tower’s foundation bolts are unused and their packing labels carry today’s date; the maintenance worker’s city-repair list remains unchecked.

premises: The tower bolts are still in their packaging.
The city-repair list on the workbench has no completed marks.
argumentForm.conclusion: A finished-looking tower does not by itself repair the damaged city.

bossPhases.title: The Final Uncertainty
bossPhases.scene: Nozick offers a final switch: within the Machine, every party member can experience a perfect answer to every question. Outside, mistakes remain possible, but your decisions will have unscripted effects. The Machine refuses to tell you whether the outside world is original.
bossPhases.question: What principle guides your reply?
bossPhases.hint: Ask whether certainty without agency could answer the final ethical question.
bossPhases.clue: The Machine guarantees subjective certainty, not that any answer corresponds to what happens outside.

options.text: Refuse guaranteed answers, preserve the freedom to investigate, and accept responsibility for uncertain real choices.
options.reflection: The party rejects forced satisfaction while admitting uncertainty about the world beyond.

loreCard.corePrinciple: The value of a life can include its activity and relation to reality.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The party rejects forced satisfaction while admitting uncertainty about the world beyond.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Some agents may reasonably prefer simulation under oppressive real conditions.

options.hiddenPremise: Living freely is not equivalent to receiving perfect impressions.
options.consequence: The party reaches the exit chamber without surrendering judgment.

options.text: Ask which world permits genuine care for others and accountable relationships, then choose without claiming that every alternative is worthless.
options.reflection: Care provides a serious reason for choice without guaranteeing one universal outcome.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Relationships and responsibilities are central components of a good life.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: Care provides a serious reason for choice without guaranteeing one universal outcome.
loreCard.strongestObjection: Relationships may themselves be possible within simulations.

options.hiddenPremise: Meaningful caring can help guide decisions under uncertainty.
options.consequence: The party keeps room for different reasons in the final vote.

options.text: Accept the guaranteed answers because freedom to be mistaken can never add value to a good life.
options.reflection: The offer assumes that certainty outranks all other values.

loreCard.corePrinciple: Knowledge and autonomy need not be traded for imposed assurance.
loreCard.sceneAnalysis: The offer assumes that certainty outranks all other values.
loreCard.strongestObjection: In high-risk circumstances dependable answers can be deeply valuable.

options.hiddenPremise: Eliminating the risk of error justifies surrendering judgment.
options.consequence: The Machine preserves the party’s certainty but erases its choice.

bossPhases.observation: A display beneath the final switch reads “certainty of sensation guaranteed”; the screen for conditions beyond the chamber remains blank.

premises: The switch specifies what its occupants will experience.
Its display supplies no reading from beyond the chamber.
argumentForm.conclusion: The switch can guarantee a feeling of certainty without reporting what happens outside.

debate.trigger: after the initial picks are revealed, before the roll, if eligible players chose differently
debate.prompt: Your actions disagree. Name the weakness you see in the reasoning, then keep or revise your choice.

machine.opening: “You have learned so much from doubt. Why risk living it again when I can write a kinder world?”

pleasure-pod.steady: “The Velvet Invitation: why choose uncertainty when I can give you the feeling of success?”
pleasure-pod.strained: “You have less Grip now. Let me take away the cost of mistakes.”
pleasure-pod.critical: “You are tired. I can make every choice feel right. Stay with me.”

friendship-record.steady: “The Friend Who Remembers: why choose uncertainty when I can give you the feeling of success?”
friendship-record.strained: “You have less Grip now. Let me take away the cost of mistakes.”
friendship-record.critical: “You are tired. I can make every choice feel right. Stay with me.”

architect.steady: “The Architect of Happiness: why choose uncertainty when I can give you the feeling of success?”
architect.strained: “You have less Grip now. Let me take away the cost of mistakes.”
architect.critical: “You are tired. I can make every choice feel right. Stay with me.”

earned-work.steady: “The Work That Was Never Done: why choose uncertainty when I can give you the feeling of success?”
earned-work.strained: “You have less Grip now. Let me take away the cost of mistakes.”
earned-work.critical: “You are tired. I can make every choice feel right. Stay with me.”

last-switch.steady: “The Final Uncertainty: why choose uncertainty when I can give you the feeling of success?”
last-switch.strained: “You have less Grip now. Let me take away the cost of mistakes.”
last-switch.critical: “You are tired. I can make every choice feel right. Stay with me.”

onSecondLook.steady: “A mistake. Even your best reasons can fail. Mine need not.”
onSecondLook.strained: “Once more? Every doubt takes something from you. I could end this.”
onSecondLook.critical: “There is only the next mistake, unless you hand the judgment over to me.”

machine.beforeBoss: “My garden is not a prison if every resident feels free. Why insist on a door?”
machine.onVictory: “Perhaps you want more than pleasure. But the final choice is still yours.”

insight.title: Lived Agency
insight.description: Your actions can matter beyond how they feel.

victory: The exit chamber opens. Nozick does not decide for you; the party must choose the life it values.
failure: The Machine draws you into a perfect dream. Your Grip returns, but you face this same decision again.
